1.title: Compute, Containers and Serverless
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Compute, Containers and Serverless. This module covers task statement three point three, identifying the A W S compute services. You will learn when to choose virtual servers, containers or functions, and how load balancing and auto scaling make an application elastic. Expect many exam questions that describe a need and ask you to name the service.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Match E C two instance families, such as compute optimized and storage optimized, to workloads. Explain what Elastic Load Balancing and Auto Scaling do, and how they give elasticity. Tell Amazon E C S, Amazon E K S and Amazon E C R apart. Choose between A W S Fargate and A W S Lambda for serverless compute. And recognize Elastic Beanstalk, Lightsail, A W S Batch and A W S Outposts.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater Needs Compute That Flexes
1.text: Tidewater's shop runs on a few big servers, sized for the holiday peak, and when one crashes, the shop goes offline. Traffic spikes at the sale and then falls. Every photo upload needs a small thumbnail, and the developers want no servers for that job. The team is packaging the shop in containers and wants help running them. And the warehouse needs local processing, right next to its scanners. Your job is to choose the compute for each need.

1.title: Compute Choices: How Much Do You Manage?
1.text: Think of compute as a spectrum, from most control to least to manage. At one end are virtual servers. Amazon E C two gives you the most control, and the most to manage. Next come containers. Amazon E C S and Amazon E K S run packaged applications, and A W S Fargate removes the servers. At the far end is serverless. Fargate and A W S Lambda mean no servers to provision or manage. Remember the shared responsibility model from Module three: the more A W S manages, the less you patch. So you choose by the control you need, against the work you want to avoid. Exam tip: most control means E C two, and least to manage means Lambda, with containers and Fargate in between.

1.title: Amazon EC2: Virtual Servers in the Cloud
1.text: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud, or E C two, provides on-demand, scalable computing capacity, in the form of virtual servers called instances. You launch as many or as few as you need, scale up for busy periods, and scale down afterward. An Amazon Machine Image, or A M I, is a preconfigured template with the operating system and software. The instance type sets the C P U, memory, storage and network capacity. Amazon E B S volumes keep data, while instance store volumes hold temporary data that is deleted when the instance stops or terminates. A security group is a virtual firewall, and a key pair is secure login information. And remember: you manage the guest operating system and its patches. Exam tip: virtual servers where you control the operating system means Amazon E C two.

1.title: EC2 Instance Types: Match the Family to the Workload
1.text: The exam wants you to match the instance family to the workload. General purpose instances give a balance of compute, memory and networking, such as for web servers. Compute optimized instances are for compute-intensive work on high performance processors, like batch processing, media transcoding and scientific modeling. Memory optimized instances deliver fast performance on large data sets held in memory. Storage optimized instances are for high, sequential read and write access to very large data sets on local storage, with many low-latency random I O P S. And accelerated computing instances use hardware accelerators for graphics, floating-point or pattern matching work. A name such as C seven G dot X large shows the family, the generation and a size. Exam tip: compute optimized for processing power, and storage optimized for local disk speed.

1.title: Elastic Load Balancing: Sharing the Traffic
1.text: Elastic Load Balancing automatically distributes incoming traffic across targets, such as E C two instances, containers and I P addresses, in one or more Availability Zones. It checks the health of its targets and sends traffic only to healthy ones. It scales its own capacity as traffic changes, which raises availability and fault tolerance. An Application Load Balancer handles H T T P and H T T P S traffic, at layer seven. A Network Load Balancer handles T C P and U D P traffic, at layer four. A load balancer can also take over encryption and decryption, using certificates from A W S Certificate Manager. Gateway Load Balancers exist, and the Classic Load Balancer is the previous generation, but both are beyond the guide. Exam tip: spread traffic across servers and skip the failed ones, and the answer is a load balancer.

1.title: Auto Scaling: Elasticity on Demand
1.text: Amazon E C two Auto Scaling keeps the right number of instances for the load, in an Auto Scaling group. You set a minimum, a desired capacity and a maximum, and the group never goes outside them. Look at the figure. Scaling policies add instances as demand rises and remove them as it falls. That is elasticity. The group also replaces unhealthy instances and balances them across Availability Zones. New instances register with the load balancer automatically, and there is no additional fee for Auto Scaling itself. A W S Auto Scaling, with scaling plans, also covers other resources. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, the documentation shows how to migrate those plans to scaling policies, so the older name may appear in study material. Exam tip: adding and removing servers automatically as demand changes means Auto Scaling.

1.title: Containers: Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS and Amazon ECR
1.text: A container packages code and its dependencies so it runs the same way everywhere. Three services work with containers. Amazon Elastic Container Service, or E C S, is fully managed container orchestration, to deploy, manage and scale containerized applications, using task definitions, tasks and services. Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service, or E K S, is fully managed Kubernetes. A W S manages the control plane, and it runs in A W S and in your own data centers. Choose it for Kubernetes. Amazon Elastic Container Registry, or E C R, is a managed registry, to store, manage and share container images, with image scanning. Think of it as the image library. Exam tip: Kubernetes means E K S, A W S container orchestration means E C S, and storing images means E C R.

1.title: AWS Fargate: Containers Without Servers
1.text: A W S Fargate runs containers without servers, or clusters of E C two instances, for you to manage. It works with Amazon E C S. You package the application, set the C P U and memory, and launch it. There is no choosing server types, no deciding when to scale a cluster, and no packing the cluster. Each Fargate task has its own isolation boundary, so it does not share the kernel, C P U, memory or network interface with another task. It is serverless, pay-as-you-go compute for containers, and new tasks always start on the latest patched platform revision. Exam tip: containers with no servers to manage means A W S Fargate.

2.title: AWS Lambda: Run Code Without Servers
2.text: A W S Lambda runs your code without provisioning or managing servers. You write a function and connect a trigger, such as Amazon A P I Gateway, Amazon S three, Amazon S Q S or EventBridge. Lambda scales automatically, and manages capacity, scaling and patching for you. You pay for requests and execution time, with no upfront commitment. A single invocation can run up to fifteen minutes, with one hundred twenty-eight to ten thousand two hundred forty megabytes of memory. So Lambda suits short-lived, event-driven work. Exam tip: running code when something happens, with no servers, means A W S Lambda.

2.title: Elastic Beanstalk, Lightsail and AWS Batch
2.text: Three more compute services appear in the in-scope list. A W S Elastic Beanstalk lets you upload application code, and it provisions E C two instances, and sets up load balancing, health monitoring and scaling. Choose it to deploy a web app without building the infrastructure. Amazon Lightsail offers virtual private servers, containers, databases, storage and networking for a low, predictable monthly price. Choose it for a simple website or a small project. A W S Batch runs batch computing jobs at any scale, provisioning the compute each job needs. Choose it for large queued jobs, with no batch software to manage. Elastic Beanstalk itself has no additional charge; you pay for the resources it creates. Exam tip: upload code and let A W S build the environment means Elastic Beanstalk; simple and predictable means Lightsail.

2.title: AWS Outposts: AWS Infrastructure on Your Premises
2.text: A W S Outposts extends A W S infrastructure, services, A P Is and tools to your own premises. An Outpost is a pool of A W S compute and storage at your site, and A W S operates, monitors and manages it as part of an A W S Region. You can run E C two instances, E B S volumes, E C S clusters and R D S databases there, with the same A P Is as in a Region. Use it for low latency and local data processing. A service link connects the Outpost to its Region. It is a hybrid deployment option, as in Module six. Exam tip: A W S-managed infrastructure inside your own data center means A W S Outposts.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: Compute
2.text: Here is how the exam frames compute. Compute or storage optimized: processing power, or fast local disk access. Load balancer or Auto Scaling: spread the traffic, or add and remove servers. E C S, E K S or E C R: A W S orchestration, Kubernetes, or the image library. Fargate or Lambda: containers with no servers, or functions with no servers. Beanstalk, Lightsail or Batch: upload code, a simple predictable server, or queued jobs. Outposts: A W S hardware in your data center. And elasticity: capacity that follows demand, up and down. Exam tip: name the need, then pick the smallest service that meets it.

2.title: Design Check: Tidewater's Compute Plan
2.text: Now a design check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Servers that grow for the sale and shrink afterward: an E C two Auto Scaling group, behind a load balancer. Spread traffic and skip a failed server: Elastic Load Balancing. A report that holds a huge data set in memory: a memory optimized instance. A thumbnail for every photo upload, with no servers: A W S Lambda, triggered by Amazon S three. The shop's containers, with no servers to manage: Amazon E C S on A W S Fargate. A team that already runs Kubernetes: Amazon E K S. A small blog at a low, predictable price: Amazon Lightsail. And local processing at the warehouse, with A W S tools: A W S Outposts. Pause the video if you want more time.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. E C two gives virtual servers, and its families match workloads, such as compute optimized and storage optimized. For elasticity, a load balancer shares traffic across healthy targets, and Auto Scaling adds and removes instances. For containers, E C S orchestrates, E K S runs Kubernetes, and E C R stores images. For serverless, Fargate runs containers without servers, and Lambda runs functions on events. The simple options are Elastic Beanstalk, which deploys uploaded code, Lightsail, which is simple and predictable, and Batch, which runs queued jobs. And for hybrid, Outposts puts A W S infrastructure in your data center.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Tidewater runs a nightly job that converts product videos to new formats, and the job is limited by processing power. Which E C two instance family fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, compute optimized. These instances are designed for compute-intensive work, and media transcoding is a listed example. Memory optimized instances target large in-memory data sets, storage optimized instances target local disk throughput, and general purpose instances suit balanced workloads.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Select two. Which two statements about E C two instance families are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are B and D. Storage optimized instances serve workloads with high sequential access to local storage, and memory optimized instances serve large in-memory data sets. Processing large data sets in memory describes memory optimized, not compute optimized. General purpose instances balance resources, and accelerated computing instances add hardware accelerators.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Tidewater's traffic spikes during the sale and falls afterward. Which service automatically adds E C two instances when demand rises and removes them when it falls? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, Amazon E C two Auto Scaling. It changes the number of instances between the minimum and maximum you set, which is elasticity. A load balancer spreads traffic without adding or removing instances, Outposts is A W S hardware at your site, and Lightsail offers fixed plans.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Which service distributes incoming traffic across E C two instances in more than one Availability Zone and sends requests only to healthy targets? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D, Elastic Load Balancing. It distributes traffic across targets in one or more Availability Zones, and routes only to healthy ones. Auto Scaling changes the number of instances, Fargate runs containers, and E C R stores container images.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Tidewater is packaging its shop in containers on Amazon E C S and does not want to provision or manage servers or clusters of E C two instances. What should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, A W S Fargate. It runs containers without servers or clusters for you to manage. E C R only stores the images, Batch is for queued computing jobs, and E C two would leave the team managing the cluster.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Every time a customer uploads a product photo to Amazon S three, Tidewater needs a thumbnail created automatically, without running any servers. Which service fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, A W S Lambda. It runs code in response to events such as an upload, needs no servers, and charges only for requests and execution time. An always-on instance, a Lightsail server or a Beanstalk environment would all keep servers running.

2.title: Practice Question 7
2.text: Question seven. Tidewater's developers want to upload the code of a web application and have A W S provision the instances, set up load balancing and scale the environment. Which service fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, A W S Elastic Beanstalk. You upload the code, and it provisions the instances and configures load balancing, health monitoring and scaling. Batch runs queued jobs, Outposts is A W S infrastructure at your site, and E C R is an image registry.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all seven answers. Question one: C. Question two: B and D. Question three: A. Question four: D. Question five: B. Question six: C. Question seven: A. That completes Module seven. Next, Module eight covers the storage services: objects, blocks, files and backups.
